structure: stand-up anecdote with plausible cartoon causality (KayfabeTip 1: therefore/but, never and-then, not verbatim): the action figure tells how the kid who owns him ran a wrestling federation in the living room; every card is the next caused or twisted event (sister, mom, dog, cousin); callbacks dog -> real injury, arm -> outro
bestOfReason: 1-4: the heads as gimmicks, the sister as crowd, the jobber is his own head.
9, 13, 14, 11: learning to sell, noise, mom's ban, the sister oversells.
30, 31, 53: empty house, the dog as crowd track, the cousin as smark.
35, 55: the dog's real bite and the family's silence.

omitted.5-8: big-body archetypes repeat the roster joke
omitted.23-29: cut for length; 29 overlaps the tweener
omitted.32-34: plant, shooter, sandbag cut so 35 carries 'real'

orderReason: Deck order kept except: the oversell clown 11 comes after the stomp punch as the overdone counterexample; the jobber's power returns as the final card beat.

cards.cardText: The Babyface, high-flying moves; audiences cheer, a slave to approval.
The Heel, eye pokes; if they aren't booing, you aren't doing your job.
The Tweener, you don't ask for it, so they want you more.
The Jobber, isolated and picked apart; you exist to make the other guy look good.
The Master Seller, reel back, limp to the ring, make them believe.
The Thigh Slap, a loud sound suggests high impact; an audio lie.
The Oversell Clown, flying backwards from a gentle tap.
The Booker, spider in suit; the ending is pre-planned, you are just a puppet.
The Empty Arena, pausing for a pop that never comes.
The Green Screen Crowd, audio sweetening on a lie.
The Internet Smark, psychology without ever taking a bump.
The Real Injury, unplanned; the crowd goes nuts because it's real.
The Kayfabe Police, keep the secrets secret, or get fired.
The Finisher, the Leg Drop; if this hits, go home.
The False Finish, the art of the near-fall.
The Retirement Match, rising, and falling; see you next season.
